name: Chinese lanterns
grown_as: A hardy perennial grown for its orange autumn 'lanterns', used in dried flower arrangements. Also sold as Physalis alkekengi (the garden form var. franchetii). Spreads strongly by underground stems.
habit: Upright, unbranched stems 40 to 60 cm, in a spreading patch from creeping underground stems. Dies down in winter.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, often in pairs of unequal size near the top
leaf.outline: Broadly oval to diamond-shaped, 5 to 12 cm
leaf.base: Wedge-shaped, running down into the stalk
leaf.margin: Entire or with a few shallow, wavy, blunt teeth
leaf.veins: Pinnate, 4 to 6 pairs of side veins

flower.form: A small open star or wheel, nodding
flower.petals: Five, joined, with five broad shallow pointed lobes
flower.centre: Greenish-yellow centre with five yellow stamens
flower.behind: A small green five-toothed calyx that grows after flowering into the lantern
flower.carried: Singly on curved stalks from the leaf joints, hanging down beneath the leaves

fruit: The calyx swells into a papery, five-angled lantern 4 to 6 cm, with a pointed tip and a sunken base, green turning bright orange-red in autumn and hanging from the stem in a row. Inside is a round orange-red berry about 1.5 cm. Over winter the lantern skin rots away to a lacy net of veins round the berry. Seeds tiny, flat, pale.
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves; first true leaves simple and oval. Usually grown from divisions, not seed.
winter: Stems die back; dead brown stems may stand with skeleton lanterns of lacy veins showing the berry inside. New shoots from underground stems in spring.

leaf: a broad oval pointed simple leaf
edge entire or with a few wavy teeth
bloom: a small creamy white five-lobed star, nodding
young: growing as a patch from underground stems
flower: hanging singly beneath the leaves on curved stalks
crop: bright orange-red papery lanterns hanging along the upper stem
each lantern five-angled with a pointed tip
dormant: bare stems with lacy skeleton lanterns
a red berry showing inside the net of veins

look_alikes: Tomatillo has yellow flowers with dark blotches and green husks filled by the fruit. Cape gooseberry has a smaller brown husk and is soft-hairy.
